title: How to Choose The Best Answering Service For Roofers
summary: Homeowners still pick up their phone to call a roofer and book a job. That's why it's more important than ever to have a proper answering service.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Homeowners still pick up the phone (a lot). If nobody answers on your end, they just call the next roofer on their list. A good answering service picks up every time, ignores the robocalls, and turns a real inquiry into a booked job instead of a voicemail you don’t listen to until the next day.


With all of the human and AI answering services out there, choosing the right one for your business can be a daunting task. For a lot of homeowners, this is their first point of contact with your business. The last thing you want is for them to have a crappy experience. The best answering service for a roofing contractor does three things:


1. **It answers every call,** even the ones that hit while you're two stories up with a nail gun.
2. **It filters spam** , so your callback list is homeowners, not scammers.
3. **It turns that call into a booked appointment,** not a sticky note on your dash.


Everything else is a nice-to-have.


## **Your phone is still the front door**


Roofers love to talk about texting, DMs, and web forms. We do it too. But homeowners haven’t got the memo. Phone calls are still the number one way homeowners prefer to reach a contractor before or during a project, with[54% saying it’s their top choice](https://roofr.com/gated-content-thank-you/homeowner-report-2026) , ahead of text and email combined.


If your "communication strategy" is to send every call to voicemail while you're on a roof, you've built a front door that only opens sometimes. And when homeowners can’t get in, they’ll move on to the next roofer on their list.


## **The 40% you're losing before you even quote**


Roughly[40% of homeowners hire the first roofer who calls them back](https://roofr.com/gated-content/soti-2025) . Not the best roofer. Not the cheapest. The first one to answer. Every missed call is a coin flip you didn't even know you were losing. And the roofer two exits down who happened to pick up just won a job because (and only because) they actually answered their phone.


## **Voicemail is not a strategy**


A few solutions roofers lean on, and why they don't hold up:


- **Voicemail and a callback later.** By the time you're off the roof, that homeowner has already called three more roofers. You lost the job before you’d even heard of it.


- **A cheap call-forwarding trick.** Great, now your spouse or your lead installer is fielding spam calls and sales pitches for solar panels between actual jobs.


- **"My office manager handles it."** Fine, until they’re on lunch, on another call, or out sick. Then there's no backup.


- **Ignoring spam and hoping it stops.** It won't. Every unscreened line is an open invite for robocalls.


None of these are a sustainable system. They're a hope and a prayer with a ringtone.


## **What a real answering service actually needs to do**


When choosing the best answering service for your business, you need a few specific features. Before you hand your business line to anything, make sure it clears this bar:


1. **Answers 24/7** , not just during business hours. Storms don't wait for your calendar to open up.


2. **Screens out spam** so your callback list is real leads, not robocalls.


3. **Recognizes your existing customers** and gets them to a human fast. Nobody wants to answer robot trivia questions about a leak they already discussed with you.


4. **Gets enough information** to provide a quote and actually book an appointment, not just say "someone will call you back."


5. **Logs the call as a real record** you can follow up on (preferably as a Job in your CRM), instead of a name and number scrawled on the back of a shingle sample.


## **Where most answering options fall short**


Human-staffed answering services can check a lot of these boxes. But they're expensive, and most weren't built for roofing. That means calls get generic scripts instead of anything homeowners recognize as credible.


AI answering tools are cheaper, but a lot of them stop at "took a message." If you go this route, make sure it can provide a quote, book a site-visit, and talk to whatever system you're already using to run your jobs. Otherwise, you're reviewing and re-typing everything anyway.


If you're evaluating options, ask this one question: does this answering service get you a booked, qualified lead, or just a slightly fancier voicemail?


## **What about the "it's a robot" objection?**


Two worries come up a lot: homeowners getting bad information from a bot, and contractors trying to hide that AI picked up at all.


Most AI answering services are trained on specific scripts and talking points, so they won’t say anything you don’t approve ahead of time.


And homeowners really don't care if a human or an AI answered — they care whether they got an accurate answer, a real estimate, and a time on the calendar. Being upfront that AI took the call costs you nothing. But giving someone a wrong quote or leaving them on hold can cost you the job.


## **Missed calls = lost business**


Every missed call is a job you didn't know you lost. Fortunately, the fix isn't complicated. It's having constant coverage, spam-screening, and a system that actually books jobs instead of just taking messages. Roofers who treat their phone like a real sales channel close more of the calls they're already getting without adding headcount.

## **FAQs: Answering services for roofers**


### ‍ **Do homeowners still call roofers, or do they prefer text and online forms?**


54% of homeowners' prefer phone calls as the top way to reach a contractor during a roofing project, ahead of text messages and email. Online forms and texting matter, but they don't replace a phone that gets answered.


### ‍ **How much does a missed call really cost a roofing business?**


It's hard to put a dollar figure on a call you never got back, but roughly 40% of homeowners hire the first roofer who responds to them. Every missed call is a job that went to someone else who actually picked up.


### ‍ **What's the difference between a human answering service and an AI one?**


Human-staffed services are typically more expensive and harder to scale during storm season, since you're paying per minute or per call. AI answering tools are usually cheaper and available around the clock, but quality varies widely. Some can only take a message, while more capable ones can screen spam, send quotes, and book appointments.


### ‍ **Can an answering service book an appointment or just take a message?**


It depends entirely on the tool. A basic call-answering service just records a message for you to follow up on later. A more capable one can walk the homeowner through a quote and get an appointment on the calendar during the call itself. You’ll know it happened when you see it on your calendar or in your CRM.


### ‍ **Is it worth paying for spam screening specifically?**


If your business number is on trucks, yard signs, and Google listings, then absolutely yes. Those numbers attract a steady stream of junk calls. Screening spam out means every call that reaches you is worth your time.
